script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 7. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Tonight, when you look up at the stars, you're looking at your ancestors.  Not metaphorically—literally.  Every atom in your body except hydrogen was forged inside a dying star.

Stars spend most of their lives fusing hydrogen into helium. As they age, they fuse helium into carbon, carbon into oxygen, and so on up the periodic table. Our sun will make it to carbon. Bigger stars forge iron. Beyond iron? Only supernovas have enough energy. The iron in your blood, the calcium in your bones, the gold in any jewelry you wear—all of it was created in supernova explosions.  When massive stars die, they explode with the energy of 100 billion suns, scattering their elemental creations across space.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You're not in the universe—you ARE the universe.  A part of it that became conscious, that can look back at the stars and wonder.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Cosmic Perspective - Zooming Out.

Here's your activity: Tonight, spend 3 minutes looking at the stars (or if cloudy, imagine them). Consider that some of that light has traveled millions of years to reach you. Let that perspective inform one thing you're stressed about. This helps you practice seeing your life from a larger perspective.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what stars are made of can be applied to cosmic perspective - zooming out. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
